title: ID0483926-DC/Si-D/NL-[RVP/T5170004768] Charger limited to 40kW
description:
Reported behaviour/issue:
We have a 400kW Siemens charger installed at our customer's location. For the past week, it has been charging at 400 kW and then dropping back to 40 kW.
Can you identify the cause of this problem and what we can do about it?
Since the customer currently does not have access to the charger via a PC, is it possible for the customer to monitor what is being charged?
It concerns the firm :
Harcotom BV
Visserijweg 20
1646 AR Purmerend
Serial number Charging station : RVP / T6170004768
Serial number Dispenser : F2RD421360

additional_info.subject: Storing Lader
additional_info.body:
Goedemiddag,
Wij hebben bij onze klant een 400kW Siemens lader staan nou laad hij de laatste week met 400 kW en valt dan terug naar 40 kW.
Kunnen jullie zien waar dit probleem aan ligt en wat we hier aan kunnen doen.
Dan heeft de klant nu geen toegang tot de lader met een PC is het mogelijk dat de klant zelf ook kan mee kijken wat er geladen  wordt ?
Graag hoor ik uw reactie .
Het betreft de firma
Harcotom BV
Visserijweg 20
1646 AR Purmerend
Serial nummer Charging station : RVP / T5170004768
Serial number Dispenser : F2RD421360
Met vriendelijke groet,

4054Bj
Charger address/functional location:  Netherlands
Priority:
Medium
Handover reason: Faulty Converter E17
Following the report of the client, we see that converter e17 is faulty. See the attached screenshot of the log:
Please check the following steps. The following are the three possible solutions for this problem:
Check the CAN cables attached to that converter. If properly connected, proceed to the next step.
Try swapping the converter that shows the issue with the one beside it. This confirms if the problem lies in the cables or in the converter itself. If the issue remains after swapping, it confirms that the converter itself is faulty.
Replace the converter.
Kindly pick up the case using "Pick" option in the queue or manually using the "Assign" function from the
eMobility RC-NL SI E Queue
and work on it & document the activity (Logs/Field Service Report) and attach it to the case under Documents Tab on ISP.
In case you require Expert Support, kindly create Work-order as per
unified service process
. If you need assistance with ordering Expert Support, feel free to reach out to Sousa, Afonso (SI E CS SD) at
afonso-sousa@siemens.com

rui.teodoso@siemens.com

Kindly close the case post resolution following the case handling guidelines.

additional_info.subject: case update
additional_info.body:
During the site visit, we spoke with the customer, who indicated that the charger initially starts at 400 kW but rapidly drops to around 40 kW after about 10 minutes. They operate two types of trucks, MAN and Mercedes-Benz. This issue happens frequently with the MAN trucks.
Today, we only had the Mercedes-Benz truck available for testing. We observed that the power limit dropped from 400 kW to 330 kW, but this was being controlled by the truck itself. From a hardware perspective, there are no issues with the charger—everything is functioning as expected. We also checked the liquid-cooled cable, and there was no sign of overheating.
Based on our observations, we suspect that the MAN truck reduces the charging limit in order to protect the battery from overheating. The charger is not always limited to 40 kW; the actual limit varies and is sometimes higher.
Additionally, the charger was commissioned last year, and the cable reel is defective. The client is still waiting for a replacement, which should be covered under warranty.
